title: Engraved plate
rule: A steel-engraved catalogue plate: figures and objects numbered and named in a lettered key ('Fig. 4, the key').
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p96_engraved_plate.py (engraving puppets and pen set: kit/build_page03.py; window and stranger behind glass: build/p49_epic.window_board)

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

made: the page as PLATE XCVI inside an embossed plate-mark with a pen double rule, headed 'RANDOLPH STATION, VT. - THE TICKET OFFICE, SEPT. 1937' and 'The figures of the afternoon, numbered in the order of their use.'

ten numbered figures, each lettered 'Fig. n.' beneath: 1 memo, 2 agent risen from his desk, 3 window with the stranger behind its glass, 4 wall clock at 4:10, 5 agent looking up and pointing to it, 6 stranger leaving, 7 cupboard open on its left jamb, 8 the brass key and SERVICE tag enlarged, 9 agent pencil to chin, 10 SERVICE door
puppets: page 03's ENGRAVING PUPPETS (Harper's 1863 telegraph operator, pinned at the joints and re-posed; the 1867 Steinway Hall woman; the 1863 table and window), with their cream scissor margins

the set drawn in the shared pen line with HANDMADE engraver's hatching: parallel pen strokes clipped to each surface (clock case, cupboard interior and door leaf, key shank, door panels, cast shadows and floor strips)
a lettered KEY TO THE FIGURES in two columns naming each figure in order and quoting the four canon lines verbatim; no balloon
key: Fig. 1. The memo on his desk: '4:15 - open SERVICE door. Key in cupboard.'
Fig. 2. The agent, risen from the desk, setting off for the cupboard.
Fig. 3. The stranger at the ticket window: "Pardon me — have you the right time?"
Fig. 4. The office wall clock, at ten past four.
Fig. 5. The agent, looking up at it: "Ten past four, by the clock."
Fig. 6. The stranger, leaving the window: "Much obliged!"
Fig. 7. The cupboard, its door opened on the left jamb.
Fig. 8. The brass key on its hook, tagged SERVICE (enlarged).
Fig. 9. The agent before the open cupboard, pencil to chin: "Well, here I am... and what for?"
Fig. 10. The SERVICE door, which stays closed; the key stays on its hook.
beat: the plate is filled in order: empty plate and heading, then figures two at a time with their key entries

self_check.check: A reader finds numbered figures and a key that names them.
self_check.evidence: perceptually judged by the maker at full size after the repair re-render: ten 'Fig. n.' labels and ten matching key entries, all legible
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker

weaknesses: the puppets are 1863/1867 wood engravings, not steel engravings; the 'steel plate' is carried by the plate-mark, pen hatching and lettering
figures are separate specimens, so the narrative (he answers her, he stands before the cupboard) is carried by number order and the key rather than by staging
the agent puppets keep page 03's cream scissor margins, so they read as cut-outs laid on the plate
Fig. 4 is the clock, not the key (the rule's 'Fig. 4, the key' is read as an example of the format)
the sheet fibre is a little softer than on the other LoC-sheet pages (repair to meet the 1.2 MB ceiling); size margin is about 20 KB
repair: 2026-11-18: the LoC sheet's finest fibre softened (0.4 sheet + 0.6 Gaussian sigma 1.8, tone and mottling kept; pen hatching, puppets and lettering untouched), page re-rendered and re-encoded at JPEG quality 90 (1,261,601 -> 1180434 bytes); master and beats b01-b06 re-rendered
